query: The Fourth Cake {Mabel's has three kinds of cake. Today, on a plate beside them, there is a fourth. "Experimental," says Mabel. "Free, if you're brave, petal."|Another fourth cake. Mabel has started a little card for each one: name, date, survivors.|The fourth cake. Mabel slides it across before you've asked; you have a reputation for bravery, or greed.} {This one is blue.|This one is suspiciously plain.|{season == "winter": It smells of cloves and something like snow.|It's still warm and very slightly humming.}} Be brave and try it {It tastes exactly like the first warm day of spring. Mabel writes "a triumph" on her card.|It tastes of your grandmother's kitchen, or a kitchen you wish had been hers. Mabel watches your face and nods, satisfied.|It tastes like good news. Mabel says this one's going on the menu, and names it after the face you made.} {It tastes of a memory of being scolded. Mabel takes it back, apologising, and writes "no" on her card.|It tastes of nothing at all, so completely that it's alarming. Mabel looks crestfallen.|It tastes of rainy afternoons in a waiting room. You can't explain it and never want to again.} Stick with your usual {You order your usual. Mabel sighs, and cuts it a little larger than usual anyway, as if to make up for your cowardice.|You stick with the lemon slice. Mabel feeds the experiment to a delighted first-year, who turns briefly blue.|"Your usual, petal?" Mabel already has it on a plate. The fourth cake waits for someone braver.}
